channel_sources:
- conda-forge
channel_targets:
- conda-forge main
docker_image:
- quay.io/condaforge/linux-anvil-x86_64:alma10
python_min:
- '3.11'

about.description:
Prothon represents a protein conformational ensemble as a vector of
probability distributions over local order parameters -- contact numbers,
virtual bond and torsion angles, solvent accessible surface area -- and
measures the Jensen-Shannon distance between corresponding distributions.

Because the representation is local, no structural superposition is
required and the cost is linear in the number of frames rather than
quadratic, which makes ensembles of tens of thousands of conformations
tractable.

Every result is reported beside its noise floor: the distance between two
disjoint halves of a single ensemble, which is the smallest difference the
sampling can resolve. A difference below that floor is reported as
unresolvable rather than as a small difference.

The method is described in Aina, Hsueh and Plotkin, J. Chem. Inf. Model.
2023, 63 (11), 3453-3461.

name: prothon
raw_meta_yaml:
schema_version: 1

# This is the reference copy. Once the staged-recipes pull request merges, the
# package is built from the conda-forge feedstock at
# https://github.com/conda-forge/prothon-feedstock, and the two have to be kept
# level in both directions -- see the note in the FastMDXplora recipe, which
# says why at length.
#
# **The conda package is `prothon`; the PyPI distribution is
# `prothon-ensembles`.** PyPI's `prothon` was registered in December 2020 by an
# unrelated protobuf generator and names there are permanent. conda-forge's was
# free, so the conda package carries the name in the 2023 paper and the source
# is fetched under the name PyPI would give it. The import name and the command
# are `prothon` either way, so the divergence is invisible to a user after
# installation and appears only in the install line.

context:
  name: prothon
  # PyPI normalises the sdist filename to underscores. The directory segment
  # tolerates either form; the filename does not.
  pypi_name: prothon_ensembles
  version: "2.4.0"

package:
  name: ${{ name|lower }}
  version: ${{ version }}

source:
  url: https://pypi.org/packages/source/${{ pypi_name[0] }}/${{ pypi_name }}/${{ pypi_name }}-${{ version }}.tar.gz
  sha256: 4570111268f28cb33c900b1bcf843776ab56705f2184eb3273e7e72ff5e3a068

build:
  noarch: python
  number: 0
  script: ${{ PYTHON }} -m pip install . -vv --no-deps --no-build-isolation
  python:
    entry_points:
      - prothon = prothon.cli:main

requirements:
  host:
    - python ${{ python_min }}.*
    - pip
    - setuptools >=64
    # The sdist carries both PKG-INFO and a generated _version.py, so the
    # version resolves without a git checkout. setuptools-scm is still a build
    # requirement because pyproject declares it in build-system.requires.
    - setuptools-scm >=8
  run:
    # Upper bound matches requires-python in pyproject.toml.
    - python >=${{ python_min }},<3.14
    - numpy >=1.22
    - scipy >=1.9
    # matplotlib-base rather than matplotlib: only the plotting library is
    # used, and the full package would pull a GUI toolkit into an install that
    # writes figures to files.
    - matplotlib-base >=3.5
    # Imported by prothon.core.plotting for PCA, MDS and t-SNE. Version 2.0
    # imported it without declaring it, which is why a clean install of that
    # release failed on the code path the CLI took by default.
    - scikit-learn >=1.0
    - mdtraj >=1.9.7
    # Arrived with config-as-study in 2.2: a study is written to and read from
    # a YAML file, and the CLI's --config and --save-config both go through it.
    # Missing here, `pip check` in the test section reports it and a user
    # installing from conda-forge would meet it as a ModuleNotFoundError the
    # first time they touched a config.
    - pyyaml >=5.1
    # mdtraj declares netcdf4 in its own Python metadata and conda-forge's
    # mdtraj does not install it, so `pip check` in the test section reports a
    # broken requirement that belongs to a dependency rather than to us.
    #
    # Adding it is the honest fix rather than disabling the check. Prothon
    # reads whatever mdtraj reads, and AMBER NetCDF is one of the formats an
    # ensemble arrives in; without netcdf4 mdtraj falls back to scipy and warns
    # that the path is significantly slower. FastMDXplora carries it for the
    # same reason.
    - netcdf4

tests:
  - python:
      imports:
        - prothon
        - prothon.core
        - prothon.core.dissimilarity
        - prothon.core.representation
        # The paths those two moved to in 2.3. `prothon.core` is a shim that
        # forwards with a DeprecationWarning until 3.0, and testing both the
        # old and the new names is what keeps the shim honest -- it shipped
        # once handling `from prothon.core import x` and not
        # `import prothon.core.x`, which this section caught.
        - prothon.compare.dissimilarity
        - prothon.represent.order_parameters
        - prothon.sampling.correlation
      python_version:
        - ${{ python_min }}.*
        - "*"
  - script:
      - prothon --version
      # Prints the order parameter registry and the detected backends, so
      # this fails if a runtime dependency is declared but does not resolve.
      - prothon --info
    requirements:
      run:
        - python ${{ python_min }}.*

about:
  homepage: https://github.com/aai-research-lab/Prothon
  summary: Software for accurate comparison of protein conformational ensembles
  description: |
    Prothon represents a protein conformational ensemble as a vector of
    probability distributions over local order parameters -- contact numbers,
    virtual bond and torsion angles, solvent accessible surface area -- and
    measures the Jensen-Shannon distance between corresponding distributions.

    Because the representation is local, no structural superposition is
    required and the cost is linear in the number of frames rather than
    quadratic, which makes ensembles of tens of thousands of conformations
    tractable.

    Every result is reported beside its noise floor: the distance between two
    disjoint halves of a single ensemble, which is the smallest difference the
    sampling can resolve. A difference below that floor is reported as
    unresolvable rather than as a small difference.

    The method is described in Aina, Hsueh and Plotkin, J. Chem. Inf. Model.
    2023, 63 (11), 3453-3461.
  license: MIT
  license_file: LICENSE
  repository: https://github.com/aai-research-lab/Prothon
  documentation: https://prothon.readthedocs.io/en/latest
